title: The Mass, again
hookLine: every scene now has a name you know
tomorrow: can a string of beads turn into a road?

cards: Here's what a first-timer like Mia will see, walking in cold. A bowl of water by the door that people touch before they cross themselves. A bell, maybe smoke.

Everyone standing, then sitting, then standing again, saying lines the whole room seems to know by heart. To someone new, it's a blur of senses. At this point on the path, every one of those scenes has a name.

teach.b: Walk it by the senses. First, the gathering: cold water at the door, the sign of the cross, a procession, a plea for mercy.
Then the table of the word: readings, a psalm sung back, and the Gospel, when everyone stands to listen.
Then the table of the bread: gifts carried up the aisle, and in some parishes incense rising, with the old line from the Psalms: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight."
Then the consecration, bells in some churches, the room on its knees, and communion. Last, the sending: go out.
One to tell a friend: the Church's instruction on the Mass describes two main parts, the Liturgy of the Word and the Liturgy of the Eucharist, joined so closely they make one act of worship.
That's the Emmaus story in miniature.
Two disciples walk with a stranger who opens the scriptures to them; then, at the table, Luke says, they told "how they knew him in the breaking of bread." Word, then bread.
The same order every Sunday. Knowing the names doesn't make the Mass less mysterious. It means you know where you are inside it.

how: Catholics attend Mass on Sundays and holy days: the Introductory Rites, the Liturgy of the Word, the Liturgy of the Eucharist and the Concluding Rites. Visitors are welcome to sit, stand and listen; Catholics who are not receiving, and guests, may stay in the pew during communion.

joined so closely they make one act of worship: word, then bread.
incense is part of every single Mass
some parishes use it, some don't; the Psalm line ties it to prayer rising.

games.q: Mia, at her first Mass, whispers as the room rises: 'why is everyone standing now?' the book's just been carried up. quickest true answer?
o: 'it's the end. everybody's getting ready to leave.'
'it's communion. stand and get in line with us.'
'it's the Gospel, Jesus's own story, so people stand to hear it.'
games.why: people stand for the Gospel, the high point of the table of the word. communion and the sending come later.

practice: Count the Mass on your fingers, naming each scene under your breath: the gathering, the readings, the Gospel, the gifts, the consecration, communion, the sending.
At each finger, call up one sense from it: the cold water, a voice reading, the bread in a hand. If you pray, end on the Emmaus line: they knew him in the breaking of bread.

wordCard.voice: The Mass. Word, then bread, the Emmaus road every Sunday, and now every scene with a name.
